text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Some police and prominent businessmen have been implicated in a spate of tobacco thefts that have hit central Malawi where most of the leaf is grown, a Tobacco Association of Malawi official said on Tuesday.

- The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party has joined government in refuting allegations of police brutality and arbitrary arrests of striking civil servants who started their action six weeks ago.
- Teachers in three of the country's key cities on Tuesday joined a six week-old civil servants strike and have vowed not to relent until their demands are met.

- Shops were temporarily closed and offices abandoned as hundreds of people scattered in all directions when about a dozen police on Tuesday fired shots in the air and teargassed striking civil servants to disperse them from demonstrating in a Bantyre street.
- Government will have to come up with K15 million ($1 million) in taxpayer's money to replace the presidential motor convoy, State House sources said on Tuesday.

- Senior scientists from nearly 40 commonwealth countries on Tuesday began their three-day-long 19th biennial meeting of the Commonwealth Science Council (CSC) in Lilongwe, the administrative capital.

- Malawi Congress of Trade Unions (MCTU) president Ken Mhango, reacting to government's letter to the Norwegian Confederation of Trade Union refuting allegations of police brutality, said on Tuesday the government was being run by immature people who fail to solve minor problems without politicising them first or lying over them.

- Police in Zomba said on Tuesday they had arrested five criminals suspected of being involved in a spate of armed robberies in the district. An AK-47 rifle and 11 rounds of ammunition was also seized.

- As pressure mounts from the donor community and the civil servants strike, government has dissolved one parastatal organisation, the National Celebrations Council and laid off 17 employees including its chief executive.
